root_cause.text: The `nf_conncount` subsystem updated the `list->last_gc` timestamp during every connection addition in `__nf_conncount_add` rather than only when garbage collection was actually executed, allowing high packet rates to continuously reset the timer and bypass garbage collection.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` being moved out of the connection addition block (under `add_new_node`) and into the preceding block where garbage collection is performed. Additionally, the commit message states that "last_gc is being updated everytime a new connection is tracked... With a sufficiently high packet rate, it is possible to always bypass the GC, causing the list to grow infinitely."

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the vulnerability by adding `list->last_gc = (u32)jiffies;` inside `__nf_conncount_add` (line 194 of the diff). This updates the `last_gc` timestamp on every connection addition, rather than only when garbage collection is actually executed. Under high packet rates, this continuously resets the timer, causing `time_is_after_eq_jiffies` to remain true and bypass garbage collection via `goto add_new_node;` (line 132 of the diff).
